summary: Suniti Kumar Chatterji was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Scottish Church College, Presidency University, Calcutta, London, and Paris under Jules Bloch. He was Khaira Professor at Calcutta (1922–1952) and National Professor in Humanities (1965–1977).
Supree Kanjanapisarn is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Assumption University under the supervision of Veerachart Nimanong (attested 2011).

Surama Dasgupta was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Surendranath Dasgupta, earned degrees from the University of Calcutta, and completed a PhD at the University of Cambridge in 1948. She was a Reader at the University of Lucknow.
Surendra Man Bajracharya is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Tribhuvan University under doctoral supervisor Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya and co-supervisor Ranjana Bajracharya.

Surendranath Dasgupta was an Indologist and philosopher educated at Calcutta and Cambridge under J. M. E. McTaggart and James Ward. His appointments included Principal of Sanskrit College (~1931–1942) and Chair of Philosophy at Calcutta (~1942–1945).
Surendranath Majumdar Sastri was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied under traditional teacher Hara Prasad Sastri. He served as a Reader at Patna University (attested 1924).
Surya Das works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University at Buffalo (1967–1971) and trained under traditional teacher Nyoshul Khenpo Rinpoche (~1984–1999).

Surya Kanta was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Frederick William Thomas and completed a D.Phil. at Oxford in 1937. He served as Reader in Sanskrit at the University of the Punjab (attested 1939).

Suryakumar Bhuyan worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Presidency University, University of Calcutta, and SOAS (PhD 1936), serving as Principal of Cotton University (1918) and Vice Chancellor of Gauhati University (~1960–1961).

Suryanarayana Shukla was an Indologist, linguist, and philosopher who studied at Rajgopal Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya under Nandakishore Pandey, Ramanujacharya, and Shridatta Pandey. He served as a professor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.
Susan Andrews is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. She earned her PhD at Columbia University (attested 2013) under doctoral supervisor Chün-fang Yü.
Susan J. Rosenfield is an Indologist who completed her PhD at Harvard University in 2004, where she studied under teachers including Stephanie W. Jamison and George L. Hart.
Susan L. Beningson is a scholar of sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Columbia University (attested 2009) under doctoral supervisor Robert E. Harrist, Jr.
Susan L. Huntington is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She served as a professor at Ohio State University from around 1970 to 2014.
Susan Meinheit is a scholar of Tibetology who held a post at the Library of Congress (attested 1998 and 2007).

Susan Naquin is a historian and sinologist who studied at Stanford and Yale (PhD 1974). She taught history at the University of Pennsylvania (1977–1993) and served as a professor at Princeton University (1993–2013).

Susan Neiman is a philosopher who studied at Harvard (PhD) and the Free University of Berlin. She held professorships at Yale and Tel Aviv University before becoming Director of the Einstein Forum in 2000.
Susan Niditch is a scholar of religious studies who held a faculty post in the religion department at Amherst College from approximately 1978 to 2020.

Susan Whitfield is a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and sinology who earned her PhD at SOAS (1995). She directed the International Dunhuang Project (1993–2017) and is a professor at the University of East Anglia.

Susanne Hoeber Rudolph was an Indology scholar who earned degrees from Sarah Lawrence, Harvard, and Radcliffe (PhD 1955). She taught at Harvard (~1954–1963) and served as a professor at the University of Chicago beginning in 1964.
